purpose: Levoketoconazole is used to treat adults with Cushing's syndrome, a condition where your body makes too much of a stress hormone called cortisol. Having too much cortisol can cause weight gain, high blood pressure, high blood sugar, and other serious health problems. This medication helps bring your cortisol levels back down to a safer range.
how_it_works: Your body makes cortisol in your adrenal glands, which sit on top of your kidneys. Levoketoconazole works by blocking certain enzymes in those glands that are needed to produce cortisol. Think of it like putting a speed limiter on a car — it slows down how much cortisol your body is churning out so your levels return closer to normal.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, headache, swelling in your legs or ankles, abnormal liver enzyme levels (detected by blood tests), tiredness, high blood pressure, low potassium levels, and changes in your heartbeat. Some people also notice decreased sex drive or adrenal insufficiency (your body making too little cortisol).
warnings: This medication can cause serious liver damage — your doctor will regularly check your liver with blood tests. It can also affect your heart rhythm (QT prolongation), so tell your doctor about any heart conditions or other medications you take. It must NOT be taken with many common drugs because it can cause dangerous interactions. Women who are pregnant should not take this medication. Your cortisol can sometimes drop too low (adrenal insufficiency), which can be life-threatening — watch for extreme tiredness, dizziness, or nausea and contact your doctor right away if these occur.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 150 mg taken by mouth twice a day (morning and evening) with or without food. Your doctor will gradually adjust your dose based on your cortisol levels and how you are tolerating the medication, up to a maximum of 600 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
